1.?

Consider the equation 3tan⁡(3x2)+1=0 for 0∘≤x<360∘. If the exact solutions x1,x2 and x3 are written in ascending order, what is the numerical value of x2+x3?

H
Wed, Jul 29th @ 10:33 AM|Elapsed: 19:49Correct

First, we rearrange the equation as follows: 3tan⁡(3x2)+1=03tan⁡(3x2)=−1tan⁡(3x2)=−13tan⁡(3x2)=−33

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

3x2=−30∘+n⋅180∘

Solving our equation for x, we get

3x=−60∘+n⋅360∘x=−60∘3+n⋅360∘3x=−20∘+n⋅120∘.

We set n=0,±1,±2,…, until we have generated all solutions in the domain 0∘≤x<360∘.

  • Setting n=1 gives x=100∘

  • Setting n=2 gives x=220∘

  • Setting n=3 gives x=340∘

All other values of n generate solutions outside the domain 0∘≤x<360∘. So, the solutions x1,x2 and x3 (written in ascending order) are x=100∘,220∘,340∘.

Finally, the numerical value of x2+x3 is 220+340=560.

2.?

Consider the equation tan⁡2x=1 for 0≤x<2π. If the exact solutions x1,x2,x3 and x4 are written in ascending order, what is the value of x1+x4?

Wed, Jul 29th @ 1:04 PM|Elapsed: 8:14Correct

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

2x=π4+nπ.

Solving our equation for x, we get

x=π8+nπ2=π8+4nπ8x=(1+4n)π8.

We set n=0,±1,±2,…, until we have generated all solutions in the domain 0≤x<2π.

  • Setting n=0 gives x=π8

  • Setting n=1 gives x=5π8

  • Setting n=2 gives x=9π8

  • Setting n=3 gives x=13π8

All other values of n generate solutions outside the domain 0≤x<2π. So, the solutions x1,x2,x3 and x4 (written in ascending order) are x=π8,5π8,9π8,13π8.

Finally, x1+x4=π8+13π8=14π8=7π4.
